links.comparator_used: Original radiology reports (500 chest X-ray reports) versus GPT-4 PRECISE-generated sixth-grade-level patient summaries
links.outcome: Readability of radiology reports (Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog Index, ARI), plus reliability and understandability ratings
links.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 38.28 to 80.82; Gunning Fog 13.04 to 6.99; ARI 13.33 to 5.86 (all p<0.001). Clinical volunteers found 95% of summaries reliable; non-medical volunteers rated 97% as fully understandable.
links.tradeoff: About 5% of summaries were not judged reliable by clinical volunteers. The authors state the approach adds no significant burden to radiologists.
links.quote: Readability scores significantly improved, with the mean Flesch Reading Ease score increasing from 38.28 to 80.82 (p-value < 0.001), the Gunning Fog Index decreasing from 13.04 to 6.99 (p-value < 0.001), and the ARI score improving from 13.33 to 5.86 (p-value < 0.001).

design_hint: reading-level constraint on LLM patient summaries with clinician reliability review
